A flat world map showing the continents in pale green and the oceans in light blue. The five oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic) are clearly labelled in bold dark blue text. The Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf of Guinea are labelled with smaller text and arrows pointing to their locations.

A world map specifically focusing on Ocean Currents. Red arrows indicate warm currents (e.g., Gulf Stream, Agulhas, Kuroshio). Blue arrows indicate cold currents (e.g., Canary, Benguela, Labrador, Peru). The arrows form distinct circular gyres: clockwise in the North Atlantic and North Pacific, anti-clockwise in the South Atlantic, South Pacific, and Indian Ocean.

A cross-section of a waterfall. A river flows over a layer of hard rock that sits on top of softer rock. The softer rock is eroded backwards (undercutting). Water plunges down, swirling rocks at the base to form a deep rounded plunge pool.
